raw_response:
I'm 55 years old, and I've been working these plots in Quzhou since I was a boy. I only went to primary school, so I don't bother with those extension leaflets — I learn by watching my own fields and listening to my neighbors. I've got about 6 mu total. Four mu I'll do wheat and maize back-to-back, like most folks around here. The other two mu I'll plant cotton — it brings more cash per mu than grain, though it's more work.

For the wheat, I'll sow in early October with my own saved seed, about 30 jin per mu. Before planting I'll run the rotary tiller over the field, then spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's roughly 100 jin. Come spring, if the wheat looks yellow at green-up, I'll topdress another half bag. I irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if the rain doesn't come. Water costs more every year with those new meters, so I don't overdo it. For weeds and bugs, I spray herbicide once and insecticide two or three times, and maybe fungicide once if I see disease.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I've got maybe five or six days to get the maize in the ground. No time for ploughing — I plant no-till, same as my cousin does. I buy the hybrid seed from the shop, Nongda 372, one small package per mu. Costs about 60 yuan per mu, but the yield is worth it. I put one bag of compound fertilizer down at planting, then irrigate twice — at tasseling and grain filling. Herbicide once, and insecticide once or twice for the corn borer. Last year I got about 550–600 jin of maize per mu, and I expect about the same this year if the weather holds.

The two mu of cotton I'll plant in late April with Guoxinmian improved seed from the shop. I'll rotary till first. Cotton is greedy — I put down almost two bags of compound fertilizer across the season. I irrigate three times and spray for insects nearly every week in summer, maybe 12 times total, plus herbicide once. It's expensive and tiring, but the cotton price is better than grain. If I'm lucky I'll get around 450 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I thought about doing more cotton, but last year the bollworm was bad and I spent too much on spray. Better to keep most land in wheat-maize — that rotation is steady, and I always have grain at home.
